Here's the draft. I haven't created anything on GitHub. I also searched the working directory for password-reset code and found none, so the details below are general and not tied to specific files.

---

**Title:** Password reset fails for email addresses containing a plus sign (`+`)

**Labels:** `bug`, `auth`

### Description
Users whose email address contains a plus sign (for example `jane+work@example.com`) can't reset their password. These addresses are valid under RFC 5321/5322, and many people use them for sub-addressing (filtering mail by tag).

### Steps to reproduce
1. Create an account, or use an existing one, with an email like `user+test@example.com`.
2. Go to the **Forgot password** page.
3. Enter `user+test@example.com` and submit.
4. Check the inbox, and if an email arrives, click the reset link.

### Expected behavior
A reset email goes to `user+test@example.com`, and the link lets the user set a new password.

### Actual behavior
<!-- Fill in the observed failure mode, e.g.: -->
- [ ] No reset email arrives (account not found / silently ignored), **or**
- [ ] The email arrives but the reset link is invalid or expired, or says "user not found", **or**
- [ ] A validation error rejects the email address on the form

### Likely cause (to investigate)
The `+` is probably being turned into a space somewhere along the way:
- **URL encoding:** If the email goes into a query string (e.g. `/reset?email=user+test@example.com`), form/URL decoding reads `+` as a space, so the lookup becomes `user test@example.com`. The value should be encoded with `encodeURIComponent` (or equivalent), giving `%2B`. Better still, keep the email out of the URL and rely only on the reset token.
- **Input validation:** An overly strict email regex may reject `+`.
- **Normalization mismatch:** The email may be normalized differently at signup and at reset (e.g. `+tag` stripped in one place but not the other), so the lookup misses.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The password reset flow works end to end for addresses containing `+`.
- [ ] Reset links don't depend on an unencoded email in the URL.
- [ ] Automated tests cover reset with `+` and other valid special characters (`.`, `-`, `_`, `'`).
- [ ] Other email-based flows (signup verification, login, email change) checked for the same problem.

### Environment
<!-- Browser/OS, app version, environment (prod/staging) -->

### Impact
Affected users are locked out of self-service account recovery and have to contact support.

---

Before filing, fill in **Actual behavior** with the failure you're actually seeing, and add the environment details. If you want it created, give me the repo and I'll file it.
